# FDG3086

> DO NOT use abbreviations or numeric indices for operator overload parameter names.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.7.1 Naming Operator Overload Parameters.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG3086
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Do not use a numeric index in the operator parameter name '{0}'

FDG3086 reports a parameter of an externally visible user-defined operator or conversion operator whose name ends with a digit, such as d1 and d2. A name equal to its type's name apart from case, such as vector3 for Vector3, is not reported. Abbreviations are not checked, because they cannot be told from words. Renaming a public parameter changes the public API for callers that use named arguments, so the fix is breaking; FDG3086 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
// incorrect parameter naming
public static bool operator ==(DateTimeOffset d1,
                               DateTimeOffset d2);
```
